text:
GENERATE BURST KP-B1a — the FIRST IMAGE of the Crucible arena: the burning cathedral's NAVE, painted at plate scale over a geometry guide (Run KC2-PLAY, Wave 2; conductor gandalf; Matt gate G-IMG satisfied, ledger KP-17; rulings KP-14 interior nave, KP-18, KP-19 "art leads the boundary"). task_id "KP-B1a".

WHAT THIS IS. One painted ground-plate chunk, 1536x1024, for a hand-painted 2D ARPG arena. The camera looks down at 52.95 degrees (an elevated three-quarter view), screen-up is NORTH. The chunk is the NORTH END of a ruined gothic cathedral's nave, seen from inside: the chancel. In the real scene the player (a 1.9 m figure) walks on this floor and fights waves of monsters here. Scale is exact and must be respected: 1 m EAST = 100.6 px across the screen; 1 m SOUTH = 80.3 px down the screen (that difference IS the camera tilt). The chunk covers 15.3 m east-west and 12.8 m north-south of floor.

IMAGES.
IMAGE 1 (1536x1024) — the GUIDE to paint over in EDIT mode: a flat tan floor plane at the exact scale, with red discs where floor hazards (burning pitch pools) are suggested. Everything in this image is scale-true; nothing in it is a boundary.
IMAGE 2 (1536x1024) — the ANNOTATION overlay: a 1 m ground grid (100.6 px across, 80.3 px down), the measured Grim-Dawn-era arena's SUGGESTED north boundary and gate gap drawn dashed, the frame origin cross at the gate (768, 799). This is information for you, never painted: the boundary is only a suggestion — the art leads, the collision comes later from your painting.
IMAGE 3 — the SCALE FIGURE: the game's player character cell at exactly 115 px tall (that is 1.9 m on this floor), feet on the magenta baseline. Every doorway, pew, step, column and rubble pile you paint must be sized so that this figure is the right height beside it. Do NOT paint the figure into the plate.
IMAGE 4 — the CATHEDRAL as it appears in our own background layer: a burning gothic cathedral on a crag — one surviving spire, pointed-arch windows with fire behind them, broken flying buttresses, a shattered rose window, collapsed roof, dark smoke. This plate is the INSIDE of that building. Match its identity: the same stone, the same fire.
IMAGE 5 — the REGISTER EXEMPLAR: a native-scale crop of our existing painted cliffside level (floor, rim rock, warm upper-left light). Your painting must match this register exactly — brushwork, contour, value structure, palette temperature, the way light spills on stone — as though the same hand painted the next room.

REGISTER (frozen, every line a constraint): HAND-DRAWN painted 2D in the manner of a modern hand-animated action game — a confident dark contour line with visible taper and varying weight, painted fills in clean planes inside the line, restrained texture; clean material planes, readable silhouettes, no conspicuous brush or pixel grain. Not pixel art. Not cel-shaded. Not a 3D render. LIGHT: single key from SCREEN UPPER-LEFT; deep cool low-value ambient; readable shadows, never pure black; FIRE is the only warm, saturated source and it lives in the pools, in the window arches and on the embers. Palette: cold stone (blue-grey, ivory, brass accents) against warm fire. No source-game names, no copied characters, no text, no UI.

COMPOSE THE CHANCEL. The floor: cracked cathedral flagstones with a worn inlaid pattern down the centre line (the nave axis runs north-south through the gate cross), scattered rubble, charred pew fragments, the shattered ROSE WINDOW lying in pieces on the floor near the gate. The north end (above the gate cross): a raised ALTAR DAIS with two or three broad steps, and behind it the broken APSE WALL rising up-screen — tall pointed-arch window openings with fire glowing inside, a partly collapsed vault, fallen roof timbers leaning against the piers. The sides: arcade PIERS and their fallen sections closing the space naturally to east and west, with rubble where a wall has come down. Six pool hazards are suggested by the red discs; paint the ones inside this chunk as BURNING PITCH seeping up through broken flagstones — you may shift or reshape them a little to fit the composition, but keep them roughly where the guide puts them. Keep the boundary EASY TO READ as a player: floor you can walk on is clearly floor; walls, dais fronts, piers and rubble heaps are clearly not.

THE ONE HARD RULE FOR THE OUTSIDE: everything that is NOT inside the nave — beyond the apse wall, beyond the side walls, anything outside the building — is painted as flat pure #00ff00 (exactly, no gradient, no haze). Walls and piers may rise up-screen from their footprint (they have height; paint their faces), but where the world ends, the pixel is #00ff00. This is how the collision boundary is later read from your painting, so the green edge is the wall's outer edge.

DELIVER exactly ONE 1536x1024 image_gen result in EDIT mode over IMAGE 1. ONE retry only if: the result is not at the guide's scale (check against IMAGE 3 — a doorway or step that would dwarf or swallow a 115-px figure), the outside is not flat #00ff00, the register drifts from IMAGE 5 (photoreal, 3D-rendered, pixel-art or cel-shaded), or it does not read as the inside of IMAGE 4's cathedral — name the reason in the receipt. Copy the output from $CODEX_HOME/generated_images/... to out/b1a_nave_01.png with sha256. No code. No other files. No web.
RETURN: receipt task_id "KP-B1a"; images = the file with prompt, references and elapsed_s; calls_used = the TRUE number of image_gen calls; status DELIVERED / DELIVERED_WITH_CONCERNS / FAILED; concerns listed honestly (what you could not reconcile between scale, register and composition). Never PASS/FAIL.

IMAGE 2 — annotation overlay: 1 m grid, SUGGESTED boundary + gate, origin cross (information only, never painted)
IMAGE 3 — scale figure: the player at 115 px = 1.9 m on this floor (do not paint into the plate)
IMAGE 4 — the burning gothic cathedral from our own background layer (identity reference)
IMAGE 5 — register exemplar: native crop of our painted cliffside level (match exactly)
